title: West Coasts of Mexico and Central America

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: With the exclusion of transiting, vessels operating in the park must check in with the Mexican Navy on Isla Socorro and will be subject to inspection.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all foreign vessels and Mexican vessels over 500 gt. Pilots will board about 1 mile WNW of the SBM, as shown on the chart, and will remain on board during all discharging operations. In bad weather, vessels may be advised to proceed to Ensenada where pilots will board at a distance of not less than 3 miles from the breakwater.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Mooring and unmooring for the SBM can be accomplished 24 hours while it is restricted to daylight only for the CBM berth. The vessel’s ETA should be advised 72 hours, 24 hours, and 12 hours prior to expected arrival. The ETA reports should be sent during office hours in order for the vessel to be scheduled at the daily Port Program Meeting.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: The terminal lies within a restricted area extending off - shore between 32°20'N and 32°23'N, as best seen on the chart. Vessels should take care to avoid a submarine cable, best seen on the chart, that extends SW from the coast from position 32°19.4'N, 117°03.9'W. A rock, awash, lies 0.5 mile SW of the terminal in position 31°58.8'N, 116°51.7'W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots board in position 31°48'13.2"N, 116°39'13.8"W about 0.4 mile S of the Landfall Lighted Buoy.

items.head: Vessel Traffic Service
items.quote: A Vessel Traffic Service (VTS) has been established. Vessels should contact the VTS when 8 miles from the breakwater providing the following information: 1. Vessel’s name and call sign. 2. Last port. 3.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels and is available 24 hours. Pilots will board 1 mile E of the pier.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all foreign vessels and Mexican vessels over 500 gt. Pilots will board on the following positions: a. 22°53'00''N, 109°51'12''W. b. 22°52'00''N, 109°52'00''W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for berthing. Pilots can be contacted by VHF through La Paz and board between 0.5 and 1 mile E of the pier.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels over 500 gt. Pilots should be ordered at least 2 hours before expected arrival; however the hours of operation are between 0800 and 1400 Monday through Friday and between 0800 and 1200 on Saturday. The pilot will board within 1 mile of the Landfall Lighted Buoy in position 24°15'12.6''N, 110°19'59.4''W.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: For vessels arriving from outside Mexican waters should report, in addition to the information above, the following a. Authorization of free pratique. b. Health patent. c. List of passengers to be admitted into the country and those intending to leave with the vessel on departure. d.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and is available, as follows: 1. Monday through Friday from 0800 to 1500. 2. Saturday from 0900 to 1300. Vessels should order the pilot 2 hours prior to arrival.

notes.quote: The pilot boards within 1 mile of the central position (25°48'16.2"N., 111°17'33.0"W.) of the range line.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory, and should be ordered 2 hours prior to arrival. Pilots board in position 26°00.5'N., 111°20.2'W.

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory, and is available from 0800-1500 Monday through Friday and 0900-1300 on Saturdays. Pilots should be ordered at least 2 hours prior to arrival. Pilots will board within 1 mile of the port breakwater.

items.head: Regulations

items.head: Caution
items.quote: A restricted area, for the protection of the vaquita porpoise, lies 7 miles NE of the point, is marked by buoys, and is being expanded (2025).

items.head: Pilotage

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: The harbormaster must be notified of any changes in ETA within 24 hours prior to arrival. Departing vessels should provide the following information: 1. Health patent.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and is available 24 hours with prior notice. Pilots board about 1 mile from the anchorage area. The pilot has also been reported (2021) to board about 0.5 mile S of the Recalada Buoy as opposed to the above position. The pilot boat has been reported (2021) to be a small red and white motor boat.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all foreign vessels and for all Mexican vessels larger than 500 gt. Pilots will board in position 17°53.44’N, 102°09.04’W about 2 miles S of the harbor entrance in the vicinity of the sea buoy as shown on chart GB 655.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: All vessels wishing to navigate within the port must obtain prior authorization from the harbormaster and the VTS, and should not exceed the established speed limits. The VTS can be contacted at any time on VHF channel 14 or 16.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels over 500 gt and is available 24 hours. The pilot boarding station is in the entrance to Boca Grande in position 16°48'14.4''N, 99°53'47.4''W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels over 500 gt and is available between the hours of 0600 and 2000 on weekdays and between 0800 and 1300 on weekends and holidays. Pilots will be arranged through the VTS that operates in Puerto de Salina Cruz. See paragraph 5.32 for details. Pilots for the SPMs will board in position 16°07'00.0''N, 95°11'57.0''W.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: A restricted area, with a radius of 600m, is centered around each of the SPMs. Entry into this zone is prohibited without prior permission from VTS Center in Puerto de Salina Cruz. See paragraph 5.32 for details.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots can be contacted by VHF and board about 2 miles S of Puerto Madero Light.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for arrival and departure maneuvers, but not for shifting berths within the harbor. Pilots are available from Puerto Quetzal. See paragraph 6.5 for requesting procedures, contact information, and ETA reporting requirements.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels arriving and departing but not for shifting berths within the harbor. Pilots are available 24 hours a day and will board in the anchorage area located about 1 mile S of the breakwater or in the vicinity of the Fairway Lighted Buoy (13°54'24.0''N., 90°46'04.8''W.).

notes.quote: The pilots can be contacted on VHF channel 16.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: The use of tugs is compulsory for vessels over 500 gt for arrival and departure at a berth. The vessel’s ETA should be sent 8 days, 72 hours, 24 hours, and 12 hours in advance. The ETA message should contain the following information: 1. Vessel name. 2.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels and available by day and at night. Pilots can be contacted by VHF channels 14 and 16. Pilot will board in position (13°34.8'N., 89°52.0'W). It has been reported only one pilot available for the harbor on any given day.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels 300 gt and over. Pilots can be requested by contacting the agent’s office or VHF channel 6, 10, or 16. Vessels should call the pilot vessel 1 hour prior to arrival, on VHF channel 16, at the outer fairway lighted buoy, where the pilot will board, about 6 miles E of Isla Meanguera (13°11'00"N., 87°35'30"W.).

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: The use of a tug is compulsory for berthing and unberthing of vessels larger than 300 gt. One tug is available in the port.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory but is only available during daylight hours. Vessels contact the pilot, who is also the loading master, by VHF or by sounding three long blasts on the ship’s whistle at intervals. The pilot boards about 1 mile SW of the harbor.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Customs and Port Health officers will board vessels upon anchoring, between sunrise and sunset, to issue clearance unless prior arrangements have been made.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and is available 24 hours. Pilots board WNW of the breakwater in position 9°55'N, 84°45'W. Requests for pilots should be made by VHF 1 hour prior to arrival.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Tugs are compulsory for berthing and unberthing.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: The pilot boards at the anchorage. See paragraph in 7.23 for details.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels berthing at the pier, but not for vessels anchoring in the roadstead. The pilot boards vessels SE of the pier in position 9°57'18''N, 84°48'00''W. The pilot will take vessels at any time, but for scheduling berthing and unberthing, the time of slack tide needs to be considered.

notes.quote: Vessels Berthed Alongside Signa l Meaning One long and two short blasts Clearance papers are on board and a pilot and mooring party are requested.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but is advisable if berthing alongside. The pilot boards about 1 mile off the wharf and will take a vessel in at night under favorable conditions.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory. Pilots are requested through the agent at least 24 hours in advance; contact should be established again 1 hour before arrival. Pilots board at the entrance to the channel.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and is available 24 hours. Pilots will board in position 8°11'N, 82°49'W.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: An ETA must be given 48 hours in advance through local agents.

items.head: Caution
items.quote: The island has a penal colony on its E side; landing is prohibited without prior permission of the Panamanian government. A local magnetic anomaly was reported to exist off the S coast of Isla de Coiba between positions 14 miles SE and 12 miles SSW of Punta Anegada. Hill Rocks, comprised of two rocks awash, lies 5.5 miles WSW of Punta Anegada.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels greater than 150 gt. Although pilots are available 24 hours, berthing and unberthing are only allowed during daylight hours. Vessels request pilotage through their agents or the National Port Authority on VHF channel 12 or 16 upon arrival. Pilot will board at the anchorage, which has a depth of 7.4m, in position 8°12'24''N, 80°24'31''W.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for any vessel greater than 150 gt. The pilot can be contacted on VHF channel 15, while the port can be contacted on VHF channels 15, 16, and 17. Pilots will board in the anchorage area.

items.head: Pilotage
items.place: For All Vessels Transiting the Canal
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels in transit through the canal area, including the ports of Balboa and Cristobal. Small craft over 20m must also use a pilot. The pilot, as well as any Panama Canal Authority board- ing officers, will board the vessel in position 08°51'46.8"N, 79°29'45"W. for entry into Balboa or when commencing transit of the canal from the Pacific side.

notes.quote: For vessels entering from the Atlantic side, they will board either inside the breakwaters in the vicinity of position 9°23'10.2"N, 79°54'58.8"W or, on request, outside the breakwaters.

items.head: Regulations
items.place: For All Vessels Transiting the Canal
items.quote: All vessels greater than 300 gt or over 20m in length must be equipped with an Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponder that meets the standards set by the International Maritime Organization. As of October 2023, all vessels with a beam of 33.2m or more (including all NeoPanamax vessels) must have a permanently-installed (fixed) navigation system capable of providing Real-Time Kinematic (RTK) positioning data to a pilot plug.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory, even if not transiting the canal. See the pilotage section in paragraph 9.10 for details and contact information.
